problem.text: Let $a_1, a_2, \ldots, a_{2018}$ be a strictly increasing sequence of positive integers such that $$a_1+a_2+\cdots+a_{2018}=2018^{2018}.$$ What is the remainder when $a_1^3+a_2^3+\cdots+a_{2018}^3$ is divided by $6$?

steps.title: Where to start: compare each cube with the number itself
steps.body:
We know nothing about the individual numbers, only their sum. So the answer can only depend on the sum, which suggests that $n^3$ and $n$ leave the same remainder when divided by $6$. Check it by factoring the difference:
$$n^3-n=n(n^2-1)=(n-1)\,n\,(n+1).$$

your_turn.prompt: Why is a product of three consecutive integers always divisible by $6$?
your_turn.answer: Among any two consecutive integers one is even, and among any three consecutive integers one is a multiple of $3$. So the product is divisible by $2$ and by $3$, hence by $6$.

steps.title: Trade the cubes for the numbers
steps.body: Since each $a_i^3-a_i$ is a multiple of $6$, adding them up shows that the sum of the cubes minus the plain sum is also a multiple of $6$. So the sum of the cubes leaves the same remainder mod $6$ as $a_1+a_2+\cdots+a_{2018}=2018^{2018}$.

your_turn.prompt: Test the idea on a small case: for the numbers $1, 2, 4$, find the sum and the sum of cubes, and compare their remainders mod $6$.
your_turn.answer: Sum $=7$, remainder $1$. Cubes: $1+8+64=73$, remainder $1$. They match.

steps.title: Shrink the base
steps.body: Now we only need the remainder of $2018^{2018}$ when divided by $6$. Replace the base by its remainder: $2018=6\cdot336+2$, so $2018^{2018}$ has the same remainder as $2^{2018}$. Careful: the answer is not $2$. That is the remainder of the base, and the exponent still matters. Also careful: being even and huge does not make a number divisible by $6$; it also needs a factor of $3$.

your_turn.answer: No. Its only prime factor is $2$, so the remainder mod $6$ cannot be $0$ (or $3$).

steps.title: Put it together
steps.body: Powers of $2$ mod $6$ go $2, 4, 2, 4, \ldots$ (since $2\cdot4=8$ leaves $2$ and $2\cdot2=4$), with $4$ at every even exponent. The exponent $2018$ is even, so $2^{2018}$ leaves remainder $4$. Check: $2018^{2018}$ is even and is $1$ more than a multiple of $3$ (because $2018$ is $1$ less than a multiple of $3$ and the power is even), and $4$ is the only remainder mod $6$ with both properties. The answer is **(E)**.

wrong_choices.A: This comes from thinking that an even, very large number must be divisible by $6$. But $2018^{2018}$ has no factor of $3$, so it cannot be a multiple of $6$.
wrong_choices.C: This comes from reducing the base $2018$ to $2$ and then forgetting the exponent. You still need the remainder of $2^{2018}$, not of $2$.
